description: ScholarShield contradiction rule weights. Stamped onto every risk_flags row so a historical score stays reproducible against the config that produced it. Never edit in place after flags exist — add a new version. v2 = v1 plus DECLARED_INCOME_BELOW_CERTIFICATE; no v1 rule changed.

SIBLING_INCOME_CONTRADICTION.note: Both tolerances must be exceeded. Certificates issued months apart legitimately differ a little, and a percentage alone fires on small absolute gaps between low incomes — precisely the applicants least able to contest a flag.

GUARDIAN_INCOME_CONTRADICTION.note: Same guardian, different households. Catches the case where household resolution failed but the guardian name is identical. Within one household SIBLING_INCOME_CONTRADICTION already covers it, so this rule skips same-household pairs to avoid double-counting.

ADDRESS_CLUSTER_UNRELATED.note: Medium, not high. Joint families, tenements, and migrant-labour housing put many genuinely low-income families at one address — the equity cases named in PROJECT_REPORT.md §6.

ISSUING_OFFICE_MISMATCH.note: Weak on its own. A family that moved between certificate applications legitimately uses two offices.

DUPLICATE_CERTIFICATE_ID.note: No tolerance needed — a certificate serial number either matches exactly or it doesn't. Highest weight in the set: reuse of one certificate across applications is closer to direct evidence than an inference from declared figures.

FAMILY_SIZE_CONTRADICTION.note: Medium, not high. A family size recorded a year apart can genuinely change (a marriage, a death, a sibling moving out); disagreement is a prompt to check the certificates, not proof either one lies.

SHARED_CONTACT_UNRELATED_HOUSEHOLDS.note: Medium: a shared landline or a relative's number lent for contact purposes happens legitimately. Weighted above ADDRESS_CLUSTER_UNRELATED because a phone number is harder to share incidentally than a street address.

DEADLINE_PROXIMITY.note: Never fires alone. Siblings applying in the same admission cycle obtain certificates days apart, which is normal and not evidence of anything. Only contributes once another Tier 1 rule has already fired on the same application.

DECLARED_INCOME_BELOW_CERTIFICATE.note: The applicant's own certificate, read by OCR, shows materially more than the form declares. Needs no second application, so it covers an applicant filing alone. Only understatement fires: overstating works against the applicant. Weighted with DUPLICATE_CERTIFICATE_ID as the closest thing to direct evidence, but gated on OCR confidence and the same two-part tolerance, because a misread digit on an honest certificate would otherwise land at the top of the queue.
